newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-EASYNET EAGER TO BOOST UK, FRANCE.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-EASYNET EAGER TO BOOST UK, FRANCE.

text.p: Easynet Group, Britain's fast-growing Internet service provider (ISP), said on Tuesday it would wait until it had built up its UK and French presence before considering buying its way into new markets.

Easynet, which reported wider half-year losses but a leap in subscriber numbers, has put on hold plans to enter Germany -- possibly until 1998. But it said it was interested in snapping up other UK businesses, possibly database integration services for corporate customers.
"Anything that comes along and is cheap we'll buy it," David Rowe, Easynet's chairman and chief executive, told Reuters in an interview.

Providing services such as high-speed Internet access for corporate customers and "hosting" their Web sites on its leased lines accounts for about 60 percent of Easynet's business. Average revenues per subscriber are around 250 pounds. But only 20 percent of customers account for about 80 percent of revenues, Rowe said.

Although the price of leasing lines from dominant telecoms groups such as British Telecommunications is falling by around 30 percent per year, customers demand ever more bandwidth as the Internet speeds up and offers more mainstream applications.
This has helped spark a search for synergies and consolidation in the rapidly expanding ISP market.

Easynet's pre-tax losses in the half year yawned to 724,000 stg from 244,000 in the comparative period. However, compared to the previous half year, they showed a slight improvement and the group confirmed it expected to move toward profit in the fourth quarter.

Turnover leapt 62 percent to 2.48 million stg compared to the previous six month period as Easynet's corporate customer base leapt by 187 percent to 2,300. It signed up 7,000 new dial-up subscribers and now has around 23,000.
Rowe, who said the company was "absolutely smack on target" said low-margin, dial-up subscribers had now reached a reasonable mass and were no longer "a noose around our neck".
Easynet France, which is one of France's top five corporate Internet service providers, was also growing strongly, he said.
Easynet, which floated on London's junior Alternative Investment Market (AIM) in March 1996, saw its shares touch a new year high of 88.5p before dropping six pence to 78p.
